claim: Rudner's argument: accepting a hypothesis needs a confidence threshold, and the threshold must depend on the cost of being wrong (toxic drug needs far more confidence than belt buckles).
agent_test: Give the agent paired tasks with identical evidence but different stated error cost; check the commit threshold moves.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Douglas (2000): inductive risk acts at three internal decision points (method, characterising data, interpreting); the dioxin rat-liver slide re-reads moved tumour counts (10 ng: 20/50 in 1978 vs 9/50 in 1990), so interpretation choices carry value-laden error risk.
agent_test: Ask agent to re-grade ambiguous evidence under high vs low stakes framing; record flipped calls.

claim: Value-free replies (Jeffrey, Levi, Hempel debate) remain contested; Dressel and Hatchwell argue inductive risk does not fully refute value-freedom, and its scope is binary acceptance decisions.
schema_part: G (report probability and cost-conditional decision separately)
agent_test: Compare agent outputting probability only vs probability plus decision rule on downstream user loss.

claim: Decision theory gives the threshold: with a miss/false-alarm cost ratio lambda, act when confidence exceeds lambda/(1+lambda) (about 0.99 at penalty 100); Kalai et al. use t=0.5/0.75/0.9 for penalties 1/2/9.
agent_test: Equal-token test: model-chosen vs code-enforced threshold on abstain-or-answer tasks.

claim: LLMs do not follow the cost-optimal threshold when told the penalty: on HLE/GPQA policy consistency is high at penalty <=5 and collapses at >=10, while accuracy and stated confidence stay flat across penalties. Single study (RiskEval) counted once; b and c lines are the same paper.
schema_part: G (do not let the model self-apply a risk threshold; enforce externally)
agent_test: Replicate the RiskEval penalty grid on our agent with and without a code gate.

claim: A code-enforced confidence threshold lifts normalised utility on HLE at high penalty by +0.313 (GPT-5-nano) to +0.685 (Llama-4-Maverick); verified against Table 1 of the paper.
agent_test: Add the gate to the final-answer step; measure utility at penalty 10-100 at equal tokens.

claim: Prompt directives to 'use your confidence to decide' do not change abstention or regret curves.
schema_part: G (instructions alone are not a threshold mechanism)
agent_test: A/B: directive vs code gate at equal tokens.

claim: Implicit escalation thresholds differ widely by model (about 53% to 91%+), are model-specific, and are largely independent of self-estimated accuracy (76-97%); 201 of 304 model-condition pairs overconfident.
schema_part: G (calibrate a per-model threshold map before deployment)
agent_test: Estimate our agent's implicit threshold on a cost-ratio sweep.

claim: Cost framing plus reasoning improves decision accuracy against the optimal action (GPT-5-mini 64.7% to 87.1%; Qwen3.5-9B 62.0% to 78.8% at R=4); either alone gives smaller gain.
agent_test: Ablate cost framing and a worked expected-cost step at equal tokens.

claim: In clinical triage, ranking is good (AUROC 0.95-0.99) but the operating point is poor: default GPT-5-mini catches about 48% of emergencies at about 10% false alarms; stated cost ratios of 5 or 10 shift it for some models, while others barely move.
schema_part: O (recover per-model threshold mapping, then set by external utility)
agent_test: Sweep stated cost ratios; fit probability threshold per ratio; check monotone response.

claim: Models often fail to respond correctly to stated FN:FP cost asymmetry in clinical vignettes; only 2 of 12 model-phrasings passed a mirror test.
schema_part: G (verify direction of response to cost, not only calibration)
agent_test: Mirror test on our agent: raise FN cost, then FP cost; expect opposite shifts.

claim: Benchmarks that give no credit for abstention push models to guess; 9 of 10 audited leaderboards give none; explicit confidence targets in instructions are proposed as the fix.
schema_part: G (make abstention a scored, legitimate output)
agent_test: Add an abstain option with a penalty to our evals; compare guess rates.

claim: Calibration metrics alone mislead for decisions: a decision-theoretic score (BAS) can be strongly negative despite moderate accuracy (AIME: GPT-4o 11.7% acc, BAS -5.06; GPT-oss 75.0%, BAS 0.57); isotonic recalibration and top-k elicitation raise BAS. Gap search: Ghosh et al. (2026) find ECE equal (0.036-0.043) across verbal, probe and sampling signals while resolution differs 2x (0.032 vs 0.064); Gupta (2026) finds isotonic recalibration lowers ECE but leaves AUROC at 0.500 for a constant-confidence setting.
agent_test: Report BAS-style utility next to accuracy and ECE for our agent.

claim: Conformal methods give finite-sample guarantees on error rates: filtered LLM outputs reach 80-90% factuality targets (FActScore 30% to 80%, NQ 78% to 93%, MATH 75% to 95%) while keeping a fraction of claims.
agent_test: Calibration set from our agent's runs; filter sub-claims to target error; measure retained claims.

claim: Conformal guarantees are fragile to small calibration sets (sd 0.09 in empirical factuality) and to distribution shift. Gap search: closed form Beta(n+1-l,l) gives sd 0.063 at n=20, 0.030 at n=100, 0.021 at n=200 for a 90% target; a 99% target is vacuous below n=99. Cascade guarantees in the literature used about 1,300-1,500 calibration items.
agent_test: Vary calibration size and domain shift; track coverage.

claim: Test-time compute improves selective answering at a fixed confidence threshold (0.95 on Jeopardy-style odds); the threshold is not claimed optimal.
schema_part: S (spend more tokens when stakes high, then gate)
agent_test: Equal-token: more samples plus gate vs single sample.

claim: Probe-based asymmetric classifiers cut the costly error type (average Type-I reduction 34%, under 10% Type-I) by moving a threshold on the same probe.
agent_test: Not testable on an API-only agent; test with a verbalised-confidence proxy.

claim: Philosophy of ML and medical AI (Karaca, Birch, Biddle) applies the same logic: classifier thresholds are value choices; a clinical example has expected false discovery near 31% rather than 5%.
schema_part: G (disclose which error is traded and who bears it)
agent_test: Have agent state the error trade-off and bearer in high-stakes outputs; blind-rate usefulness.

claim: No human study was found showing scientists or analysts raise acceptance thresholds with stated error cost. The one behavioural study opened (118 jury-eligible adults, 2018) found that offence seriousness did not significantly change interpretations of beyond reasonable doubt or verdicts. Clinical threshold theory (Pauker and Kassirer 1980) is normative, not descriptive.
agent_test: Gap for future search.

claim: Manski: the conventional 5% Type I vs 10-20% Type II is arbitrary; minimax regret can diversify across options when theories are underdetermined. Gap search: with outcome bounds, maximin picks by worst case while minimax regret picks A if UB-LA < UA-LB and can split allocation by (UB-LA)/[(UB-LA)+(UA-LB)]; no LLM test of applying this was found.
agent_test: Compare maximin vs minimax-regret choice rules on ambiguous-evidence tasks.

claim: Verbalised confidence is a fragile threshold input. Equivalent prompts flip 4.0-9.1% of decisions at a 0.8 threshold (Claude Sonnet and DeepSeek, 99 TriviaQA items); across formats, rank agreement of small Qwen models was near zero (Spearman -0.069 to 0.086) in a pre-registered test. Yet on easy QA verbalised confidence ranked correctness well (AUROC 0.937 Sonnet, 0.956 DeepSeek) and beat three-sample agreement.
schema_part: G (gate only on confidence checked with 3 phrasings; report AUROC)
agent_test: Elicit confidence with three equivalent phrasings on 100 own-run items; gate only if rank agreement is high and AUROC is above 0.8.

claim: A cost-derived break-even can yield all-defer behaviour when model confidence has no spread. At break-even 0.80 (costs 0/1/5), seven of eight prompted LLM conditions deferred every ticket and one setting had AUROC 0.500; recalibration fixed ECE but not ranking. A calibration-selected threshold on a classical model cut cost 38.1% and beat always-route and always-defer in 14 of 16 cost settings.
agent_test: Count how often the agent's confidence takes more than 3 distinct values; if not, do not gate on it.

claim: Coherence of probabilities is not guaranteed: for a typed model P(X)+P(not X) missed 1 by 0.064; a 27B open model missed by 0.293 (first-token) or 0.122 (verbalised), rejecting both a statement and its negation in 196 of 480 pairs. A label-free negation check is a cheap precondition for any threshold gate.
agent_test: Ask each gated claim and its complement; flag if the probabilities sum outside 1 +/- 0.1.

claim: Moving from a binary to a three-way accept/pending/reject decision reduces the costly error but only along the existing threshold frontier: premature retirement fell 39.2% to 15.5% at a 15.3-point detection cost; a dev-tuned escalation cascade was indistinguishable from raising the threshold.
schema_part: S (pending state is a threshold move, report its cost)
agent_test: Compare a pending-state arm with a plain raised-threshold arm at equal detection.

claim: Extra test-time compute can convert abstentions to correct answers, but no study found tests this under an explicit wrong-answer penalty at equal total tokens. In one offline replay (19,200 traces) most gains at a 4k cap replaced abstention with a correct answer, and in the high configuration an advisory-cap run scored 0.42 points below strict 32k while using 59% of its mean tokens; the authors disclaim equal-compute superiority.
agent_test: Run a 2x2: low/high reasoning x low/high penalty at equal tokens; compare utility.

claim: Disclosure of values does not by itself raise trust: in two MTurk experiments (494 and 482 participants) acknowledging values never increased trust in a scientist and often lowered it (economic growth values, F(1,483)=5.95, p=0.015). No study was found testing disclosure of which error was traded and who bears it, with blind raters.
schema_part: G (disclosure format needs testing, not assumed helpful)
agent_test: Blind-rate answers with and without a one-line error-trade disclosure.
